parameters.content:
## FloodGuard flood alarm & escalation
Receives flood forecasts from the FloodGuard portal, decides an **alarm level** per forecast, keeps one alarm per forecast target in **`flood_alarms`**, and alerts by level:

| Level | From risk_class | Channels | Starts at |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Watch | Watch / Moderate / Medium | Slack | Tier 1 |
| 2 Warning | High | Slack + Gmail | Tier 1 |
| 3 Danger | Very / Extremely high | Slack + Gmail + WhatsApp | Tier 1 |
| 4 Extreme | Extreme | Slack + Gmail + WhatsApp | Tier 2 |

Probability ≥ 85 % raises a Warning-or-worse by one level. People come from the **`duty_roster`** table (on-duty officers per tier); a tier with nobody on duty is skipped. Unacknowledged alarms climb a tier (District → PDMA → NDMA) every 15–60 min; the **Acknowledge** link in each alert stops that.

Tables: `flood_alarms` (alarms) · `alarm_events` (audit trail) · `alarm_notifications` (every delivery) · `duty_roster` (who is on duty, with Gmail / WhatsApp toggles per person) · `alert_channels` (Slack / Gmail / WhatsApp toggles per level). Every alarm event is also posted to the FloodGuard backend.

**Edit settings** (Slack channels, callback URL, intervals) in **Alarm settings**.
**Gmail & WhatsApp**: wired but switched off until credentials are added (logged as `pending_auth`).
**First run**: click **Execute workflow** on *Set up & test* (bottom left): it creates the tables, fills the example roster and channels, then sends dummy forecasts.

options.renameFallbackOutput: Not sent (pending / no one on duty)

nodes.name: Send Gmail
nodes.notes: Gmail over SMTP. To switch on: add an SMTP credential (smtp.gmail.com, port 465, SSL, your Gmail address + app password) here, enable this node, then in Alarm settings set channels.gmail.fromEmail and enabled = true.

nodes.name: Send WhatsApp
nodes.notes: Credential pending. To switch on: add a WhatsApp Business Cloud credential here, enable this node, then set channels.whatsapp.phoneNumberId and enabled = true in Alarm settings.

parameters.content:
### Test stand-ins
**Mock Slack** and **Mock backend** answer like a Slack incoming webhook and the FloodGuard API, so alerts can be tested before the real ones are connected.

nodeGroups.name: Load settings & duty roster
nodeGroups.description: Reads Alarm settings, who is on duty (duty_roster) and the channels per level (alert_channels), then routes by input.

nodeGroups.name: Validate & decide
nodeGroups.description: Checks each forecast, gives it an alarm level, compares it with the open alarm and decides: raise, escalate, remind, resolve or ignore.

nodeGroups.name: Reply to portal
nodeGroups.description: Answers the portal's request: 202 accepted, 400 nothing usable or 401 wrong key, with what happened to each forecast.

nodeGroups.name: Escalate unacknowledged alarms
nodeGroups.description: Every 5 min: open alarms nobody acknowledged in time move up a tier (District, PDMA, NDMA). Tiers nobody can be reached at are skipped.

nodeGroups.name: Record acknowledgement
nodeGroups.description: The Acknowledge link in an alert marks the alarm acknowledged, which stops tier escalation, and shows a confirmation page.

nodeGroups.name: Save alarm
nodeGroups.description: Writes the alarm's new state to flood_alarms, one row per alarm.

nodeGroups.name: Notify on duty officers
nodeGroups.description: Builds one message per channel and person on duty, sends by Slack, Gmail or WhatsApp, and logs every attempt in alarm_notifications.

nodeGroups.name: Audit trail & backend callback
nodeGroups.description: Writes each alarm change to alarm_events and posts it to the FloodGuard backend; the call is logged too.

nodeGroups.name: Set up tables & test data
nodeGroups.description: Creates missing tables, adds example rows to an empty duty_roster and alert_channels, then sends dummy forecasts.
